# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Intake Brief: help screen and improved help line (WL-0MTV97GV20088CS7)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list footer advertises only a small, mixed-signal
subset of the available keyboard shortcuts — including the low-value
`d:downtime toggle` and the mouse-tracking hint `alt+m mouse on` — while offering
no discoverable reference for the full command set or for the meaning of the
icons rendered on each row. Users cannot discover what keys are available or
what the glyphs mean without reading the source.

## Users

Herdr producers and agents who navigate work items in the pane-based selection
list and rely on the footer and on-screen glyphs to operate the tool.

**User stories:**

- As a Herdr user, I want a single `?` shortcut that opens a help screen, so I
  can discover every available command without reading the source.
- As a Herdr user, I want the help screen to explain every icon shown in the
  list, so I can interpret the status, stage, priority, risk, effort, audit and
  agent glyphs at a glance.
- As a Herdr user, I want the footer help line to advertise the help screen
  rather than rarely-used toggles, so the most useful discovery path is always
  visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Footer help line updated** — In the selection list footer, the
   `d:downtime toggle` entry is no longer advertised and `?: Help` is shown
   instead. The `d` key binding itself remains functional (only its inline
   advertisement is removed).
2. **Mouse hint removed from footer** — The `alt+m mouse on` / `alt+m mouse off`
   footer hint is removed. The `Alt+m` mouse-tracking toggle itself remains
   functional and is documented in the help screen.
3. **Help screen opens on `?`** — Pressing `?` in the selection list opens a
   dedicated help screen (full-pane overlay). Pressing `?`, `Esc`, or `q`
   dismisses it and returns to the list with no state mutation (selection,
   filters, and navigation stack unchanged).
4. **Help screen lists all commands** — The help screen enumerates every
   registered shortcut available in the selection list, grouped by chord
   leader, showing the chord key(s), label and a short description. The list is
   derived from the live `ShortcutRegistry` so future shortcut additions appear
   automatically.
5. **Help screen identifies all icons** — The help screen includes an icon
   legend that identifies every glyph rendered in work-item rows (at minimum:
   status, stage, priority, epic, risk, effort, audit, producer-review, agent
   state and child-coverage icons), each with a short meaning.
6. **Graceful on small panes** — The help screen renders within the pane height
   without overflowing the `rows - 1` render budget (scroll or truncate when
   content exceeds the viewport; the dismiss keys remain discoverable).
7. **Tests** — New/updated tests verify: (a) the footer shows `?: Help` and no
   longer shows `d:downtime toggle` or `alt+m mouse on/off`; (b) the help
   screen renders the registered commands and the icon legend; (c) `?` toggles
   the help screen on and off without mutating list state.
8. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/TUI.md`, the icon legend in
   `docs/icons-design.md` (if the on-screen legend wording is authoritative) and
   any relevant README entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing chord handling: `?` must not conflict with any
  registered shortcut chord or navigation key.
- Backward compatibility: all existing shortcut key bindings (including `d` and
  `Alt+m`) continue to function unchanged; only their footer advertisement
  changes.
- The help screen is display-only/read-only — it must not dispatch commands, spawn
  panes, or mutate the worklog.
- Icon legend content must be derived from the single source of truth
  (`@worklog/shared/icons`) rather than a hand-maintained duplicate list, so it
  cannot drift.
- Must respect the existing `showHelpText` gate (when help text is disabled, the
  help screen and its footer hint are not offered).

## Existing state

- **Footer hint assembly** — `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` composes the
  footer from `formatFooterShortcutHints()` (single-key entries render as
  `key:label`) plus an explicit mouse-tracking hint appended at render time
  (`dynamicHints` around the "Mouse-tracking toggle hint
  (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)" block). The `d` entry comes from
  `src/shortcuts.json` (`chord: ["d"]`, `label: "downtime toggle"`).
- **View modes** — `ViewMode = 'list' | 'detail' | 'filter' | 'form'`
  (`worklist.ts`). `renderWorklist()` branches on mode; `filter` mode shows a
  simple full-pane prompt — the closest existing precedent for a full-pane help
  overlay.
- **Key handling** — `keyToAction()` maps navigation keys; single-key shortcut
  resolution and chord handling happen in the main key loop. No `?` handling
  exists today.
- **Icons** — all row glyphs come from `@worklog/shared/icons`
  (`statusIcon`, `stageIcon`, `priorityIcon`, `epicIcon`, `riskIcon`,
  `effortIcon`, `auditIcon`, `needsProducerReviewIcon`, `agentStatusIcon`,
  `getIconPrefixParts`/`isCoveredByParent`). `docs/icons-design.md` documents the
  icon set and accessible labels.
- **Shortcut registry** — `ShortcutRegistry.getChordEntries()` /
  `getEntriesForStage()` expose all valid entries with `chord`, `label` and
  `description`, gated by code-freeze and issue-type.

## Desired change

1. **Footer (`formatFooterShortcutHints` / render-time composition):**
   - Exclude the `d:downtime toggle` single-key entry from the footer hint (or
     suppress its advertisement while keeping the binding).
   - Prepend/insert a literal `?: Help` hint.
   - Remove the `alt+m mouse on/off` suffix block.

2. **New help mode:** add `'help'` to `ViewMode`; render a full-pane help
   overlay in `renderWorklist()` with two sections — **Commands** (grouped by
   leader, `chord → label — description`) and **Icons** (glyph → meaning) —
   respecting the pane height budget.

3. **Key binding:** in list mode, `?` toggles the help mode on; inside help
   mode, `?`, `Esc` and `q` return to the previous mode (record the
   pre-help mode, mirroring the existing `preFormMode` pattern).

4. **Tests:** extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or a focused
   `worklist-help.test.ts`) for the footer and help-screen behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `ViewMode`, `formatFooterShortcutHints()`,
  footer composition (mouse-hint block), `renderWorklist()` help overlay, key
  handling (`?`), help-content builder.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutRegistry` used to enumerate
  commands for the help screen (read-only; no signature change expected).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — icon definitions used to build the legend
  (read-only; source of truth).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — shortcut definitions; no new entry
  required if `?` is a reserved key, but a `?` entry may be added for
  discoverability.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or new
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist-help.test.ts`) — footer and help-screen tests.
- `docs/TUI.md` — document the `?` help screen and updated footer.
- `docs/icons-design.md` — icon legend reference (update if wording is
  authoritative).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut/help summary if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQDR5HZC006JWOK** — "Show available shortcut keys in browse list help
  text" (completed). Introduced the dynamic shortcut hint line this work
  extends.
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** — "help line for chord commands too verbose"
  (completed). Collapsed/trimmed chord hints in the same footer.
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** — "Stage-based shortcut condition filters" (completed).
  Added stage-aware shortcut filtering used when enumerating help entries.
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** — mouse-tracking toggle (`Alt+m`) whose footer hint
  this work removes.
- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — `/downtime toggle` command backing the `d` shortcut.
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — "Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the
  selection list" (completed). Directly related: owns the mouse-tracking
  behaviour whose `Alt+m` footer hint this work removes.
- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94** — heading/display-row model used by the renderer.
- **WL-0MTV979LK005YB1B** — footer wrap guard (relevant to keeping the help
  overlay within the render budget).

None of these are duplicates or blockers — they provide historical context for
the footer, chord and renderer subsystems.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTD0IVNN003WCOB** – Warn in wl export/import --help that export dumps the whole DB and import REPLACEs it (completed)
- **WL-0MUN4ARHA001SN40** – Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old (open)
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** – Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, alt, downtime, help, icons (+10 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — `d` binding retained:** "replace `d:downtime toggle` with
  `?: Help`" is interpreted as replacing the footer *advertisement* only; the
  `d` key continues to toggle downtime and is documented in the help screen.
- **Assumption — `Alt+m` retained:** the mouse-tracking toggle remains
  functional; only its footer advertisement is removed (documented in the help
  screen).
- **Assumption — list view scope:** the help screen is offered in the selection
  list. Detail-view command help is out of scope unless trivially reachable.
- **Risk — key conflict:** `?` must not collide with a registered chord or
  navigation key; verify against `shortcuts.json` and `keyToAction()`.
- **Risk — icon-legend drift:** hard-coding the legend duplicates the icon
  source of truth. Mitigate by deriving rows from `@worklog/shared/icons` where
  practical, or add a test asserting every legend glyph matches the exported
  icon.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full command *reference* (rendering help text for
  detail/form modes) is out of scope; record such follow-ups as linked work
  items rather than expanding this one.
- **Small-pane risk:** the combined commands + icons content can exceed short
  panes; require truncation/scroll so the footer stays one row and the render
  invariant holds.
- **Performance risk:** negligible — help content is computed only when the
  help screen is opened.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked — the work-item description and code analysis
provided sufficient detail. Assumptions above were applied where the seed
context was ambiguous and are recorded for producer review.

Discovered-from: WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH.

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. All child ACs were persisted as partial ('Ready to close: No'), which then reverted the in_review children to open/plan_complete and (via dependency reconciliation) to blocked — cascading a parent audit to 'Ready to close: No' even though the parent's own ACs were all met.

The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.

# Record the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract

## Why

The drain-before-cheap feature failed because it hardcoded a cheap-pool budget (2) that no longer matched the proxy config. The cheap pool was silently changed from 2 to 3 slots, and fast is 1 slot -- the inverse of the brief's assumption.

## Scope

- Record the current mode slot counts and where they live:
  - fast = 1 slot (`llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml`: `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; `config-fast.yaml` does not override)
  - cheap = 3 slots (`llm-manager/proxy/config-cheap.yaml`: `session_slot_pool_size: 3`)
- State the contract: client/proxy-consumer logic MUST NOT hardcode pool sizes; derive from live status or not at all.
- Note the change history (cheap 2 -> 3) and the risk of silent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The slot-count contract and both source locations are documented (README or docs/design).
- [ ] A pointer exists from the mode-switch design doc to the contract.
- [ ] No production code change (documentation only).

# Intake: Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement

**Work Item:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U
**Issue Type:** bug
**Priority:** medium
**Discovered from:** WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish`'s live-repo mutation guard (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`, consumed by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`) fails a full-suite run whenever any non-worktree ref moves during the ~17-minute run. On a multi-agent host, concurrent agent activity moves `refs/heads/dev` (another agent's finish fast-forward on the shared main checkout), `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and other `refs/remotes/origin/*` (concurrent fetch/push), and siblings' feature-branch refs — none of which the current exclusion covers. The result is a spurious 'live-repo mutation detected' verdict while the canonical suite itself passes, forcing a wasted ~17-minute run: the item resets to `open`, the agent must re-sync and re-warm the test cache before retrying. Observed twice on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `implement.py finish` or `/skill:test` on a shared multi-agent host; the guard's false positive blocks their release gate.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the finish-gate verdict as the pre-push signal for `dev`.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of `git_sandbox.py` and the two guards (F4 outer `run_tests.py`, F5 inner conftest/`live_repo_guard.py`) that share the helper.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the finish-gate full-suite run to stay green while sibling agents advance `dev`, fetch/push to `origin`, or move their own branch refs, so that concurrent activity on the shared host does not nullify a ~17-minute run.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout (the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX `GIT_DIR`-leak class), so real corruption is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want the exclusion contract documented and regression-tested at both helper and guard level, so the two consumers cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A snapshot diff in which **only** `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, or `refs/remotes/origin/*` moved (working tree and non-excluded config unchanged) reports `changed == false`; `fingerprint()` agrees. Regression tests cover each ref class (local `dev`, remote-tracking `dev`, arbitrary `origin/*`).
- [ ] AC2 — Genuine mutations are **still** detected and fail the guard: a new/removed/moved ref outside the excluded set (e.g. fixture branch creation like the 2026-09-24 incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), a non-excluded local-config rewrite, and any working-tree change. No behaviour of the existing agent-worktree / `refs/worklog/*` exclusions regresses.
- [ ] AC3 — `guarded_run_all` (the `implement.py finish` test gate) and the inner per-test guard both pass in a deterministic regression test that moves `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/dev` mid-run on a `tmp_path` sandbox, while the same harness still fails when a genuine mutation (e.g. a new non-excluded branch) is introduced.
- [ ] AC4 — The exclusion contract is documented in the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8, naming exactly which ref namespaces are excluded and why concurrent collaborative movement cannot be distinguished from suite-caused moves of those refs (residual-risk note).
- [ ] AC5 — Full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the new changes; new regression tests live with the existing guard tests (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` as appropriate).

## Constraints

Excluding a ref namespace is only acceptable where concurrent-agent movement and suite-caused movement are genuinely indistinguishable *and* the incident signature remains detectable through the other surfaces (working tree, config, non-excluded refs).
- Any extra git invocation must stay cheap and confined to the snapshot path; the per-test fingerprint must not become a full `status` scan.

## Desired change

- Extend the exclusion contract so refs that concurrent agent activity legitimately moves cannot fail the gate: at minimum `refs/remotes/origin/*` (remote-tracking refs — only `fetch`/`pull`/`push` move them, never a hermetic fixture) and the integration branch `refs/heads/dev` (advanced by siblings' finish fast-forwards on the shared main checkout). Sibling feature-branch refs are already excluded while registered as agent worktrees; handle any residual unchecked-out sibling branch movement if the implementer can do so without a `wl-*` name pattern.
- Tighter alternative (if preferred by the implementer): scope the ref-check to the refs a suite could plausibly touch (e.g. ignore ref *moves* but still report ref *additions*), while keeping config + working-tree detection intact.

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Extend the exclusion set (e.g. `refs/remotes/origin/*`, `refs/heads/dev`) in `_parse_worktrees`/`snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`; document the contract in the module docstring.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — Helper-level regression tests for dev/remote-tracking ref movement (no diff) and non-excluded ref moves (still reported).
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Guard-level tests: mid-run `dev`/`origin/dev` movement does not trip the inner guard; a genuine non-excluded ref adds/moves still fails.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` / `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — Verify `guarded_run_all` benefits from the shared fix; add a focused regression test if needed.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — §8 exclusion contract update (refs excluded for concurrency reasons + residual risk).
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — Only if the outer/inner guard needs a code change beyond the shared helper (prefer helper-only so consumers cannot drift).

## Related work

- `WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6` — source session where the false positive was observed twice (discovered-from).
- `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627` — predecessor false positive: linked-worktree anchoring; fixed by the `main_checkout_root()` helper this item builds on.
- `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` — 2026-09-26 `GIT_DIR` leak incident; the guard's reason to exist; the mutation-detection this item must not weaken.
- `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` — origin of `git_sandbox.py` (remote `dev` corruption / test isolation); snapshot design source.
- `SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H` / `SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ` — outer (`run_tests.py`) and inner (conftest) live-repo guards.
- `SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65` — superseding producer decision for the worktree-registration churn false positive (same guard path).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — incident write-up and the snapshot/exclusion contract this item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** excluding `refs/remotes/origin/*` and `refs/heads/dev` from the diff is acceptable because those refs' concurrent movement is indistinguishable from suite-caused movement, and exhaustive ref-based detection is replaced by config/working-tree/non-excluded-ref detection for those namespaces. If the producer prefers full-strength ref detection, the alternative is the tighter scoping (AC2 language) or running the suite under a repo lock.

- **Risk (scope creep):** expanding into refactoring the guard or adding a repo lock. Recorded as out of scope; a lock or serialisation idea can be linked as a follow-up work item.

- **Risk (drift):** two consumers share the helper; keep the change helper-only so `run_tests.py` and the conftest guard cannot drift (AC3).
- **Residual risk:** two agents running `finish` concurrently can still contend on the same worktree/branch; excluded at the shared-ref level here, not solved (separate concern).

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context (discovered-from:WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6) already contained the problem, observed evidence, impact, possible fix directions and a workaround. Questions below were resolved by repo investigation and recorded for auditability.

Recorded as an assumption (see Risks); preferred fix direction per the source item's "Possible fix".

# Intake Brief: Migrate downtime-worker tests from toHaveBeenCalledWith to observable-outcome assertions

**Work Item:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium

## Problem statement

Parent **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** AC4 required assertions to prefer observable
outcomes over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators
(`skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). The 13-child split preserved all
existing assertions verbatim — **137** `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences
before and after — and AC4 was deferred to this follow-up. The assertions are
therefore unreviewed: some legitimately assert the unit's observable contract
(calls to injected dependencies and boundary adapters), while others couple
tests to implementation detail (child-process event wiring) or duplicate a
behaviour already asserted through the returned outcome.

## Users

- **Maintainer / AI agent** — needs downtime-worker tests that survive
  refactoring because they assert the unit's observable contract rather than
  its internal wiring.
- **Reviewer** — needs an auditable classification showing every retained
  assertion is intentional and every migration preserves behavioural coverage.

## Evidence and baseline

Baseline across `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (commit
`b195e01a`):

| File | `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences |
|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` | 37 |
| `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` | 22 |
| `downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` | 21 |
| `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` | 15 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` | 14 |
| `downtime-worker.test.ts` | 13 |
| `downtime-worker.sprint-view.test.ts` | 8 |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` | 3 |
| `downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` | 2 |
| `downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` | 2 |
| **Total** | **137** |

(Includes 18 `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` and 8 negative
`.not.toHaveBeenCalledWith` forms; 4 occurrences are `handle.once` child-process
event-wiring shape assertions.)

Targets are mock collaborators only — the files contain **zero** `vi.mock()`
calls. The overwhelming majority of occurrences target injected `deps.*`
functions (`spawnAgentPane` 34, `claimItem` 17, `rollbackClaim` 4,
`recordDispatch`/`recordDispatchFailure` 7, tier lookups, etc.) or test-local
mock adapters injected as dependencies. A small minority target non-boundary
internals (`handle.once`) or observable output streams (`stderrSpy`) or
injected adapters (`spawnFn`, `fetcher`, `callback`).

## Scope decision (producer, Q1-A)

The producer approved this classification rule:

- **Boundary / observable contract → retain (justified).** A call on an
  injected `deps` function or an injected boundary adapter
  (`spawnAgentPane`, `claimItem`, `closePane`, `spawnFn`, `fetcher`,
  `callback`, anchors, reapers, `dep`, …) is the unit's observable contract
  because the entry points take `deps` as an argument; there is no other
  observable channel for these side effects. Observable output streams
  (`stderrSpy`) are likewise observable outcomes.
- **Internal / redundant → migrate.** (a) Implementation-detail wiring such as
  `handle.once('error'|'exit', …)` shape assertions where the same test already
  drives the listener and asserts the resulting `spawned` outcome; (b)
  redundant call-shape/query assertions whose behaviour is already proven by a
  returned outcome/state (e.g. a tier query when `outcome.kind` and
  `outcome.candidate` are asserted).
- **Ordering assertions** (`toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` proving tier/fallback
  order) are retained unless an outcome assertion proves the identical
  ordering; otherwise they carry unique behavioural coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Classification complete.** Every `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrence in
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (baseline 137) is recorded in
   a classification table posted as a work-item comment — file, line, category
   (`retain` / `migrate`), and a one-line reason — and the category counts
   reconcile to the baseline total.
2. **Internal/redundant assertions migrated.** Every occurrence classified
   `migrate` is converted so the same behaviour is asserted through an
   observable outcome (returned value/state), or removed only where an
   existing assertion in the same test already proves that behaviour.
   Verification: `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith'
   packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts` returns zero matches.
3. **Retained assertions justified.** Every retained occurrence carries a short
   inline comment stating why the dependency call is the unit's observable
   contract, and appears in the classification table (producer Q2-A).
4. **Behavioural coverage preserved.** No downtime-worker test case is deleted;
   the test-case count is unchanged; for every removed assertion the
   classification table names the outcome assertion that replaces it. Only
   `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files change (no production-code change).
5. **Parent AC4 satisfied.** An evidence comment is posted on
   WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX linking this item and its outcome; the parent is not
   reopened or re-audited (producer Q3-A).
6. **Documentation and full suite.** All related documentation and code
   comments are updated to reflect the changes; the full project test suite
   passes with the new changes (run via `/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- Do not change production code — the change is confined to
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (plus inline comments).
- Preserve test semantics; no assertion may be dropped without a named
  replacement or an explicit table justification.
- All written output in UK English.
- Do not introduce new test dependencies.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- 14 `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files (13 split files plus
  `downtime-worker.test.ts`), 137 `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences, zero
  `vi.mock()` calls.
- Shared scaffolding (`makeDeps`, status fixtures, temp-dir helpers) lives in
  `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`.
- Parent **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** is `completed`/`done`; AC4 was deferred to
  this item by producer decision.

## Desired change

Apply the producer-approved classification to every occurrence, migrate the
internal/redundant subset to observable-outcome assertions, annotate the
retained subset, publish the classification table, and close the deferred
parent AC4 with an evidence comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — largest target (37); mostly boundary deps + redundant `getNextItem` queries
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — boundary deps, `stderrSpy`, ordering assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` — boundary deps, negative assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` — tier-ordering (`Nth`) assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — `handle.once` wiring (migration target), injected `spawnFn`/`callback`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — `resumeStalledPane` boundary assertion
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.sprint-view.test.ts` — injected `dep`/`getHerdrListHead`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — injected `fetcher`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` — small boundary counts
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — source of the anti-pattern guidance (reference only; no change)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-migration weakens regression coverage.** Mitigation: every
  removal must be paired with the outcome assertion that replaces it, named in
  the classification table.
- **Risk: mechanical removal of ordering assertions hides tier-ordering
  regressions.** Mitigation: retain `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` ordering
  assertions unless an outcome assertion proves identical ordering.
- **Assumption (producer-approved):** injected `deps`/boundary-adapter calls are
  observable outcomes, not internal collaborators (Q1-A).
- **Risk: scope creep.** Do not migrate `toHaveBeenCalledWith` outside
  `downtime-worker.*.test.ts`; other test suites are out of scope (record as a
  separate work item if desired).
- **Risk: classification ambiguity.** Unresolved cases are retained with an
  explicit justification, never silently dropped.

## Related work

- **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** — Split `downtime-worker.test.ts` and cap mocks per test (parent; AC4 deferred)
- **WL-0MV4VEQOZ005XH34** — Split settings and worker state tests into a dedicated file (split child)

  assertions already proven by a returned outcome; injected `deps`/boundary

- **Q2 — Where should retained-assertion justifications live?**

- **Q3 — How is parent AC4 "satisfied" given the parent is already

Discovered from: WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (producer-rejection fix).

The default-view refresh path opens a FRESH WorklogDatabase connection per withInProcessDb call — twice per refresh (fetchActionableCount + fetchChildrenForItems). Each open is a synchronous better-sqlite3 operation (~46-70 ms on the 100 MB worklog.db, including initializeSchema/initializeFts DDL) that blocks the TUI event loop. After the WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN loop fix (counter-only watch), refreshes are occasional so this is a transient hiccup, not continuous lag; but it violates the strict reading of the <=100 ms p95 input-lag budget when a refresh coincides with typing.

Proposal: open ONE connection per refresh, share it between the actionable-count and children reads, close in a finally; or move the in-process read off the critical render path. Keep the no-stale-cache invariant (never serve from the store's in-memory query cache across a refresh boundary) by still closing per refresh.

# Intake Brief — Don't open pane for recording reviews (WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ)

**Headline**: When a herdr selection-list shortcut declares `open_pane: false` but also contains an unknown placeholder (e.g. `a-r`'s `<reason>`), the placeholder form dialog dispatches the command without forwarding the `open_pane` flag, so a visible command pane still opens. The fix forwards `openPane` (and `onRefresh`/`focus`) through the form-dialog dispatch path so `a-r` — and any future placeholder shortcut with `open_pane: false` — runs in the background.

## Problem statement

In the herdr selection list, pressing `a-r` (audit reject) is configured in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` with `"open_pane": false`, which is supposed to run the command in the background with no pane (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL). However, `a-r`'s command template contains an unknown placeholder (`<reason>`), so it is intercepted by the form dialog (`form-dialog.ts`) to collect the rejection reason. The form dialog's `onSubmit` handler calls `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model ?? undefined)` directly, passing only two arguments and dropping the resolved `openPane` flag. As a result, a visible "Command Output" pane opens even though the shortcut explicitly opted out of a pane. Identical shortcuts without a placeholder (`a-y`, `u-p-*`, `x-c`, `x-d`) correctly run in the background, confirming the form-dialog path is the specific point of failure.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** using `a-r` (audit reject) on `in_review` items in the herdr selection list. They expect a quiet, non-intrusive rejection that just updates the item state.
  - *As a reviewer, I want to reject an item with a reason and have it recorded silently in the background, so I don't have to dismiss a command-output pane after every rejection.*
- **Herdr plugin users generally**: any shortcut entry that combines an unknown placeholder with `open_pane: false` (current and future entries) should honour the no-pane contract.

### User stories

- As a reviewer, when I press `a-r` and enter a rejection reason, the command runs in the background (no pane opens), the item is rejected, and the list refreshes.
- As a plugin author, I want `open_pane: false` to be honoured consistently regardless of whether the command has placeholders, so the flag's contract is reliable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No pane for `a-r`** — Pressing `a-r` on an `in_review` item, entering a reason in the form, and submitting results in **no herdr pane being opened**; the audit-reject command runs in the background (detached `bash -c` with output captured to a per-run log file under `<tmpdir>/herdr-background-logs/`).
2. **Form-dialog parity** — The form-dialog `onSubmit` dispatch path in `worklist.ts` forwards `openPane` (and, when present, `onRefresh` and `focus`) to `onCommand` using the same arity rules as `executeResolvedCommand`/`resolveAndRouteCommand`, so placeholder shortcuts honour `open_pane: false` exactly like placeholder-free shortcuts.
3. **Default behaviour unchanged** — Shortcuts **without** `open_pane: false` (i.e. `open_pane` omitted or `true`) that trigger the form dialog still open a pane exactly as today (no regression for `c-q`, `u-s`, `u-t`, `c-n`, `P-p`, etc.).
4. **Background lifecycle preserved** — A background form-dialog dispatch still (a) fires the existing failure toast when the command exits non-zero, with the command, exit code/signal and an output excerpt (WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV), and (b) triggers the post-completion selection-list refresh via `onRefresh` (WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T).
5. **Test coverage** — A unit/integration test exercises the form-dialog dispatch path with `openPane === false` and asserts `onCommand` receives the flag (and `onRefresh`), plus a negative test asserting the default open-pane behaviour is unchanged.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (the "No-pane dispatch via `open_pane: false`" section), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **No new dispatch mechanism** — reuse the existing `open_pane: false` background execution path (`spawnBackgroundShell` / `spawnBackgroundPi` via `index.ts`'s `onCommand`). No new flag or config key is introduced.
- **Backward compatibility** — the fix must append `openPane`/`onRefresh`/`focus` only when they are `false`/present (matching the existing "append when explicitly set" rule in `resolveAndRouteCommand`), so 2-arg `onCommand` callers and pane-opening behaviour are byte-compatible.
- **Code Freeze guard preserved** — the form dialog's existing Code Freeze guard (`readCodeFreezeState().active && isImplementCommand(finalCmd)`) must remain intact.
- **Scope boundary** — adding `"open_pane": false` to other placeholder shortcuts (e.g. quick create `c-q`) is **out of scope** for this item and is tracked by the sibling item WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4; the generic root-cause fix here naturally benefits it once that flag is added.
- **Environment assumption** — herdr plugin runtime; the worklog data store is unaffected.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` already declares `"open_pane": false` for `a-r` (audit reject), `a-y` (audit approve), `u-p-l/m/h/c`, and `x-c`/`x-d`.
- `processChordInput` (`worklist.ts`) stores `chordState.resolvedOpenPane = entry.openPane ?? undefined` when a chord resolves.
- In the chord-complete handler, `openPane` (and `focus`) are read from `chordState`, cleared, and passed through `executeResolvedCommand(...)` to `dispatchChordCommand` → `resolveAndRouteCommand`, which forwards them to `onCommand` following strict arity rules.
- **The gap**: before reaching `executeResolvedCommand`, the chord handler checks `hasUnknownIdentifiers(command)` and, when true, constructs a `FormState` whose `onSubmit` calls `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model ?? undefined)` — dropping `openPane`, `onRefresh`, and `focus`. `a-r`'s `<reason>` placeholder always triggers this path, so the flag is lost and `index.ts` falls back to `shouldOpenPane = openPane ?? true`.
- The placeholder-free quiet shortcuts never hit the form dialog, which is why they already behave correctly.
- Existing tests cover `dispatchChordCommand`/`executeResolvedCommand` openPane plumbing (`worklist.test.ts` "openPane plumbing") and the audit reject compound command routing, but **not** the form-dialog dispatch path.

## Desired change

1. In `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, in the form dialog's `onSubmit` handler, dispatch with the same arity/flag rules as `executeResolvedCommand`:
   - Resolve `<id>` and record the command as today.
   - Keep the Code Freeze guard as today.
   - Pass `openPane`, `onRefresh`, and `focus` to `opts.onCommand` (append only when `openPane`/`focus` are set / `onRefresh` is present) so `open_pane: false` and `focus: true` are honoured after form input.
2. # Intake Brief — Do not show pane for quick create (WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4)

**Headline**: The Herdr quick-create chord (`c` then `q`) always opens a visible
"Command Output" pane. Add `"open_pane": false` to the `c q` entry so the
`!!wl create` command runs detached in the background, with the selection list
refreshing on completion. The generic root-cause fix that lets *form-driven*
shortcuts honour `open_pane` is tracked separately by the blocking sibling
WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ; this item owns the `c q` opt-in, the quick-create
regression test, and end-to-end verification.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr selection list, the quick-create chord (`c` then `q`) dispatches
`!!wl create -t … -d … -p …` but always opens a visible "Command Output" pane.
The user must dismiss that pane after every quick create, even though the command
needs no visual confirmation and its result (a new work item) is visible in the
list itself. The per-shortcut `open_pane: false` feature that already makes other
shortcuts (audit approve/reject, priority updates, close/delete) run quietly is
not applied to the `c q` entry, so quick create never opts into background
execution.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** who create work items frequently via the `c q`
  chord and want the item created without a pane interrupting their browsing.

### User stories

- As a worklist user, when I press `c` then `q`, fill in the quick-create form
  and submit, I want the work item created **without a command-output pane
  opening**, so my flow is not interrupted and I can keep using the list.
- As a worklist user, I want the selection list to refresh once the background
  create completes, so the new item appears without me pressing refresh.
- As a user of any other shortcut, I want the pane-opening behaviour to be
  unchanged unless that shortcut explicitly sets `open_pane: false`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Config opt-in** — The `c q` ("create quick") entry in
   `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` sets `"open_pane": false`.
2. **Background dispatch** — Submitting the quick-create form dispatches
   `!!wl create -t '<title>' -d '<description>' -p '<priority>'` with
   `openPane === false`, so no herdr pane is spawned; the command runs detached
   in the background with stdout/stderr captured to a per-run log (existing
   `spawnBackgroundShell` path in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`). This AC is
   enabled by the blocking sibling WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ (form-dialog flag
   propagation) and must be verified end-to-end once that item lands.
3. **Refresh on completion** — After the background `wl create` exits, the
   selection list refreshes (via the existing background `onRefresh` plumbing,
   WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T) so the newly created item appears without a manual or
   periodic refresh.
4. **Regression tests** — Automated tests assert: (a) the bundled `c q` entry
   is marked `open_pane: false`; and (b) submitting the quick-create form
   dispatches with `openPane === false` (no pane) — updating the existing
   `chord-quick-create.test.ts` assertion that currently expects the 2-arg
   pane-opening call.
5. **Default unchanged** — Other, non-opted-in shortcuts (including other
   form-driven ones) still open a pane exactly as today.
6. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (the "No-pane
   dispatch via `open_pane: false`" section), and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
7. **Full suite** — The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Depends on WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** — the form-dialog dispatch path must
  forward `openPane`/`onRefresh` before a form-driven `c q` opt-in can take
  effect. This item must not duplicate that `worklist.ts` fix; it adds the
  config and verifies/tests the resulting behaviour.
- **Default unchanged:** shortcuts without `open_pane` must keep opening a pane
  exactly as today; the change only affects entries that opt in.
- **Single-instance refresh:** the completion refresh is scoped to the
  dispatching TUI instance (fire-and-forget, non-blocking); no global watcher
  and no cross-instance effects.
- **Feedback:** the background path's existing behaviour is retained — a stderr
  line with the log path at dispatch, and a toast only on non-zero exit; no new
  visible pane or modal is introduced.
- **Surgical change:** the change is the one-line config opt-in plus tests; do
  not alter the `open_pane` schema or the
  `spawnBackgroundShell`/`spawnBackgroundPi` implementations.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — the `c q` entry has no `open_pane` key,
  so dispatch defaults to opening a pane. Other quiet shortcuts (`a-y`, `a-r`,
  `u-p-*`, `x-c`, `x-d`) already set `"open_pane": false`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the form-submit closures currently drop the
  resolved `openPane` flag (calling `opts.onCommand(finalCmd, model)`), so even
  a configured `open_pane: false` would be ignored for form-driven shortcuts.
  This is **fixed by WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** (out of scope here).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — already routes `openPane === false` `!!`
  commands to `spawnBackgroundShell` and wires `onExit` → `onRefresh`; no change
  expected.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — already parses `open_pane` into
  `openPane`; no change expected.

## Desired change

1. Add `"open_pane": false` to the `c q` entry in `shortcuts.json`.
2. Add `'c,q'` to the expected no-pane set in the shortcut-config regression
   test.
3. Update the quick-create form test to assert the background dispatch
   (third arg `false` + `onRefresh`) rather than the current 2-arg
   pane-opening call.
4. Once WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ lands, verify end-to-end that `c q` creates the
   item with no pane and that the list refreshes on completion.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Dependency risk:** until WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ lands, the config opt-in alone
  will not suppress the pane; the quick-create test would need the sibling fix
  to pass. Mitigation: record the blocking relationship and sequence
  implementation after the sibling.
- **Risk — silent failure:** a background create that fails is only visible via
  a failure toast + log. Mitigation: rely on the existing
  `notifyBackgroundFailure` path; no new mechanism.
- **Assumption:** the list refresh on completion is sufficient feedback for a
  created item; no explicit success toast is required. Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`onRefresh` on background exit).
- **Scope-creep risk:** incidental improvements to the quick-create form
  (e.g. validation, issue-type selection), or applying `open_pane: false` to
  other form shortcuts, are out of scope and should be recorded as separate work
  items rather than folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — add `"open_pane": false` to the `c q`
  ("create quick") entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/chord-quick-create.test.ts` — update the submit assertion
  to expect the background dispatch (third arg `false` + `onRefresh`) instead of
  the current 2-arg call; assert no pane is opened.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — add `'c,q'` to the expected
  `open_pane: false` set in the "quiet state-change shortcuts" test.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — **not changed here**; the form-dialog flag
  propagation is delivered by WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document that `c q` is a quiet (no-pane)
  shortcut, if the README enumerates them.

## Related work

- **WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** — Don't open pane for recording reviews. **Blocking
  sibling**: fixes the shared form-dialog dispatch path so form-driven
  shortcuts honour `open_pane: false`; its scope boundary explicitly defers the
  `c q` opt-in to this item.
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — Add per-shortcut option to control whether a
  shortcut opens a command pane. The parent feature that introduced
  `open_pane: false`; its AC5 seeded the `a-y` entry but did not cover
  form-driven shortcuts.
- **WL-0MT1KB70U0012X6T** — Refresh the selection list when background
  (no-pane) shortcut commands complete. Supplies the `onRefresh` hook this item
  relies on (AC3).
- **WL-0MTCLB50D0026YA7** — Support multiple create options. Introduced the
  `c n` / `c q` chords and the quick-create form.
- **WL-0MU9LJPI5000HOR4** — Update shortcuts.json: replace c shortcut with c-n
  and c-q chords. Introduced the `c q` quick-create chord entry that this item
  makes background.
- **WL-0MLSDIRLA0BXRCDB** — Add /create OpenCode command for creating work
  items from TUI. Related create-work-item-from-TUI work (different surface,
  same user flow).
- **WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N** — Herdr selection list requires double dispatch for
  priority update to reflect. Documents the background-dispatch refresh
  suppression this item's AC3 builds on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: (No clarifying questions asked.) — The seed context was judged sufficient:
  the desired behaviour ("do not open this pane, do the work in the
  background") is explicit, and the repo already provides the `open_pane: false`
  feature and background-dispatch/refresh plumbing. Source: agent evaluation of
  `WL-0MV6J5JXL002D8C4` description and repo inspection.
- Q: Is this a duplicate of the form-path fix in WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ? — Answer:
  Partial overlap only. The sibling fixes the generic form-dialog flag
  propagation and explicitly scopes the `c q` opt-in out to this item
  (WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ, "Scope boundary"). This item therefore covers the
  `c q` config, its regression test, and end-to-end verification, and is
  recorded as blocked-by the sibling. Source: `wl show
  WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ`; `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
- Q: Should the quick create still surface the created work-item ID? —
  Research: the background path writes command output (including the new ID) to
  a per-run log file and shows a toast only on failure; the list refreshes on
  completion, making the new item visible. Assumption: this is acceptable and
  matches the "background" intent. Source: `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
  (`spawnBackgroundShell`, `notifyBackgroundFailure`, `onRefresh`).
- Q: Should shortcuts without `open_pane` change? — Answer: No; the default
  (open a pane) is unchanged. Source: WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL AC4.
- Open question: none.
## Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MV6J4HQ0009OJPQ** – Don't open pane for recording reviews (open)

# Status-neutral audit-tier claim and guarded rollback (herdr)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator running herdr downtime dispatch, I want the audit-tier claim to change only the assignee, so an audited `completed`/`in_review` item never enters a hybrid state and a failed audit can never strand it off the review queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Audit-tier claim is status-neutral: item stays completed/in_review through dispatch and failed-audit restore (`wl show` after simulated failure shows completed/in_review).
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) issues `wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""` — it writes no `--status` and no `--stage`.
- [ ] The item reads back as `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` throughout the claim (no `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid).
- [ ] `rollbackClaimWorkItem` clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`, so only this claim's state is reverted.

# Show what an item is blocked on (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8)

## Problem statement

When browsing work items in the Herdr selection list, the metadata panel shows status, stage, priority and other fields but not *what* a blocked item is waiting on. A user who sees a blocked item must leave the list (or run `wl dep list <id>` by hand) to discover the blocking work items, so the "blocked" signal is not actionable at a glance.

## Users

- **Producers / triage engineers** browsing the Herdr worklist who need to understand why an item cannot proceed.
- **Dispatch operators** who inspect a blocked candidate before deciding whether to escalate its blocker.
- **Developers** who want to see which dependency edge is holding an item up without leaving the pane.

### Example user stories

- As a **producer**, I want to see the ID and title of every work item blocking the selected item, so that I can decide whether to unblock it or prioritise the blocker.
- As a **dispatch operator**, I want the blocked-by information in the selection list metadata panel (not only the detail view), so that I can triage without switching views.
- As a **developer**, I want the blockers shown even when the item's stored `status` is still `open` (dependency-blocked), so that I am not misled by a stale status.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When the selected item has at least one **active blocker** (an outbound `depends-on` edge whose target is neither `completed`/`deleted` nor at stage `in_review`/`done`), the Herdr selection-list metadata panel renders a `Blocked By` entry at the **end of the metadata section** (after the existing metadata rows, before the description preview).
- [ ] Each active blocker is rendered as its own `Blocked By` row in the form `Blocked By  WL-xxxxxxxx — <title>`, one row per blocker, so both the ID and title are visible.
- [ ] The `Blocked By` row(s) appear for **any** selected item with active blockers, regardless of the item's stored `status` (so dependency-blocked `open` items are covered), and are omitted entirely when there are no active blockers.
- [ ] Completed/terminal dependencies (`completed`, `deleted`, `in_review`, `done`) are **not** listed as blockers.
- [ ] Blocker resolution failure is fail-open: a failed/unparseable `wl dep list` lookup yields no `Blocked By` rows and never breaks rendering or navigation (consistent with `resolveMetaLastCommand`).
- [ ] The metadata panel continues to scroll correctly (`m`/`M`) with the extra rows, and the panel never overflows its allocated rows.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: rendering one row per active blocker with ID + title; omission when no active blockers; filtering of terminal blockers; the dependency-blocked-but-`open` case; and the fail-open path.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Scope is the Herdr selection-list metadata panel only.** The detail view and the Pi TUI are out of scope; the change must not alter their rendering.
- **No new dependency edges are created or mutated** — this is a read-only display change.
- **Reuse existing semantics and helpers** where possible: `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`) for the "still blocks" predicate, and `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) for parsing `wl dep list <id> --json`.
- **Fail-open**: dependency look-up errors must degrade to "no blocked-by rows", never to a thrown error in the render path.
- **No list-data shape regression**: `WorkItem` consumers (list rows, filters, dispatch) must be unaffected by any added optional field.
- **Consistent with the metadata-panel conventions** established by `buildMetaRows`/`pairMetaRows` and the icon/label formatting (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9).

## Existing state

- The selection-list metadata panel is rendered by `formatMetadataPanel()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, which builds rows via `buildMetaRows()` (paired with `pairMetaRows()`), then appends a markdown-rendered description preview. Rows are label/value pairs; the panel scrolls independently via `metaScrollOffset`.
- `formatMetadataPanel()` is called from `createListRenderer()` with the selected row, and the renderer already receives a per-selection enrichment value (`metaLastCommand`, resolved by `resolveMetaLastCommand()` in the main loop). That parameter is the established precedent for selection-scoped data.
- `WorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) currently carries no dependency/blocker data; no `wl dep list` call is made for list items. `wl next`/`wl list`/`wl show` JSON does not include blocker edges.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` returns `outbound` edges with `id`, `title`, `status`, `priority` and `direction: depends-on`. `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` already parses this; `isActiveBlocker()` already defines the active-blocker predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` already resolves critical blockers via `wl dep list` for the downtime dispatcher (`fetchCriticalBlockers`), so the command/JSON shape is proven.
- The completed TUI work items WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU / WL-0MP15T47A001OCB1 established the "Blocking"/"Blocked by" rendering precedent in the TUI details pane; the Herdr selection list currently has no equivalent.

## Desired change

When the selection-list metadata panel renders the selected item, resolve that item's outbound `depends-on` edges, keep only the **active** blockers, and append one `Blocked By` row per blocker at the end of the metadata section:

```
Blocked By  WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W — worklist.ts: pre-dialog gate + freeze-on-confirm integration
```

- Lookup is performed for the **selected** item only (not every list row), on selection change, with best-effort caching keyed by item ID and refreshed with the list refresh; the render path must not block on it.
- The panel already scrolls, so no `+N more` truncation is required (decision Q3-A).
- No blockers → no `Blocked By` rows; the panel is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — add a `blockedBy` parameter to `formatMetadataPanel()` and `createListRenderer()`; render one `Blocked By` row per blocker at the end of the metadata rows; keep panel truncation/scroll behaviour intact.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — add an optional `blockedBy?: Array<{ id: string; title: string }>` field to `WorkItem` (or a dedicated resolver result type) and a `fetchBlockersForItem(id)` helper running `wl dep list <id> --json`, filtering via the active-blocker predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — reuse the exported `isActiveBlocker()` predicate (no change expected; import if needed).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reuse the exported `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` parser (no change expected; import if needed).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (main TUI loop) — resolve blockers for the selected item alongside `resolveMetaLastCommand()` and pass them into the renderer; fail-open on lookup error.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — tests for `formatMetadataPanel` blocked-by rendering, filtering, omission and scrolling.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` — tests for the new blocker fetch/parse helper (active filtering, terminal filtering, failure path).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the new `Blocked By` metadata rows.

## Related work

- **Herdr selection list should show dependency-blocked items (WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2)** — completed; added `--include-blocked` so dependency-blocked items appear in the list. This item makes their blockers visible.
- **Default Herdr list still hides blocked items despite --include-blocked (WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE)** — completed; mandatory blocked subset. Related because both concern blocked-item visibility.
- **Herdr in_review filter hides blocked items that the release gate treats as release-blocking (WL-0MV70XY6D008013C)** — completed; blocked-item filter semantics.
- **Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI (WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU)** and **TUI: Render dependency links in Details pane (WL-0MP15T47A001OCB1)** — completed; established the "Blocking"/"Blocked by" rendering precedent (TUI details pane). This item ports the *blocked-by* half into the Herdr list metadata panel.
- **Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9)** — completed; metadata-row formatting conventions this change follows.
- **Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)** and **Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)** — completed; the panel layout/scroll contract the new rows must respect.
- **Synthetic dispatch rows for the worklist (WL-0MUL2IY8L009S3PQ)** — completed; log-derived rows. Blockers are only meaningful for live rows; the implementation should skip the lookup for `isLogOnly`/`isLogDerived` rows.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** blocker resolution could grow into a general dependency browser (inbound "Blocking" rows, click-to-open, `+N more`). That is explicitly out of scope (decision Q1/Q3); any such opportunity should be recorded as a linked follow-up work item, not absorbed here.
- **Performance risk:** a `wl dep list` process spawn on every selection change could make fast arrow-key navigation feel laggy. Mitigation: resolve only the selected item, cache by ID, refresh with the list refresh, and keep the render path non-blocking (render the last-known/empty result until the lookup completes).
- **Fail-open risk:** a hung `wl dep list` could delay the lookup. Mitigation: apply the existing `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`/transient-retry pattern and treat timeout as "no blockers shown".
- **Assumption (Q1-A):** "blocked" means *has at least one active outbound dependency edge*, not merely `status=blocked`; this is required to cover dependency-blocked `open` items.
- **Assumption (Q2-A):** terminal targets (`completed`/`deleted`/`in_review`/`done`) are not shown as blockers, reusing `isActiveBlocker()`.
- **Assumption (Q3-A):** one row per blocker; the panel's existing scroll makes truncation unnecessary.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list` edges carry a usable `title`; when a title is empty the row falls back to the ID alone rather than rendering a dangling separator.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Which items should show a `Blocked By` row? (a) Any item with active (non-terminal) outbound dependency edges, regardless of stored `status`; (b) only items whose stored `status` is `blocked`; (c) both, but only dependency-blocked items that are also `status=blocked`." — Answer (operator): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: dependency-blocked items can still carry `status=open` (see `wl next --include-blocked`), and (a) is the only option that answers the question for those.
- Q2: "Which blockers should be listed? (a) Only active blockers (outbound deps not `completed`/`deleted` and not at `in_review`/`done`), matching `isActiveBlocker()`; (b) all outbound dependencies, including completed ones." — Answer (operator): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: consistent with the existing "still blocks" predicate; avoids noise from already-done blockers.
- Q3: "How should multiple blockers render in the metadata section? (a) One `Blocked By` row per blocker, each `WL-xxxx — <title>`; (b) a single `Blocked By` row listing all blockers comma-separated; (c) one row per blocker truncated after N with `+N more`." — Answer (operator): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: matches the established TUI details-pane precedent and keeps each blocker's ID + title readable; the panel already scrolls, so no truncation is needed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MM04HDI618Y7DT0** – Add dependency-blocker filter tests (completed)
